title: perf(canary): enhanced auto-detection and rollout guards for latency/throughput regressions
author: Ava Patel
release_notes: Improve performance canary auto-detection sensitivity and add KV-aware hysteresis rollout guards. Safer rollouts by default; reduce false positives while maintaining fast detection of regressions.
description:
Motivation: Our perf canary has been conservative and generated frequent false positives for noisy workloads (short bursts, KV-cache warmup). This change improves automated detection sensitivity while reducing noise by making detectors KV-cache aware and adding hysteresis-based rollout guards.

Summary of changes: - Add adaptive detector that considers baseline traffic distribution (p50/p95/p99) and per-model sequence-length buckets. - Introduce KV-cache-aware hysteresis so temporary KV cache misses (warmup) do not trigger rollbacks. - Add an explicit rollout_guard module that ties detection output to traffic-shift policies (canary window, step-up limits, automatic rollback). - Add end-to-end perf-lab integration tests and docs for tuning thresholds. - Expose new telemetry metrics and tags (canary_detector_version, kv_cache_state) to help debug small regressions.

Checklist: - [x] Detector algorithm implemented and unit-tested - [x] Rollout guard implementation and integration tests - [x] Perf lab e2e tests added and run - [x] Observability metrics instrumented and dashboards updated - [x] Docs updated with tuning guidance

Context & rationale: We observed two classes of noise: (1) transient latency spikes during KV cache cold starts and (2) short traffic bursts that moved sample distributions temporarily. The previous single-threshold detector triggered on P95 shifts without hysteresis, causing unnecessary rollbacks. The new detector uses dynamic baselining and per-bucket sensitivity, and the rollout guard applies hysteresis windows and requires consistent violations across consecutive windows before initiating traffic shifts.

How this was validated: Local unit tests + perf-lab runs against synthetic workloads that simulate cache warmup and short bursts. We ran a 72h canary on staging with the new guard enabled; it reduced false-positive rollbacks by ~78% while detecting true regressions within 2 canary windows in our tests.

Notes for operators: Default thresholds are conservative; ramp by editing perf-canary/config.yaml. See docs/perf-canary.md for examples. If you hit unexpected rejections, check perf_canary.detector.v=logs and the kv_cache_state tag in the canary metrics.

review_comments: Diego Ramos: Please clarify how the detector handles multi-model endpoints with different sequence-length profiles. Are buckets per-model or global?
Author (Ava): Buckets are per-model by default; updated detector to attach model_id to baseline and added fallback to global baseline when model samples are low.
Priya Nair: Concern about rollout_guard simplifying to a single heuristic; can we ensure manual abort remains immediate?
Author (Ava): Manual abort overrides automated actions; added explicit admin_abort metric and documented it. Also added tests to ensure immediate abort behavior.
Jamal Greene: CI perf-lab failed on first run (timing flakiness). Reran and all checks passed. Recommend adding retry on the perf-lab job.
Author (Ava): Added a retry with jitter to perf-lab job; reduced flakiness in our runs.
